A year ago, a small team set out with one belief. Good food does not need to be reinvented. It just needs to be discovered and given a faster way to reach people.

That belief sent them across the country, into kitchens and small manufacturing units run by people who had spent years quietly perfecting a recipe to perfection. The team worked alongside these makers who already had the expertise and supply chain in place.

A year of tasting sessions, long debates over a single ingredient, and an obsession with getting things right has led to NOICE growing into a brand with over 400 products across 20 categories, built with more than 60 manufacturing partners nationwide.

This is the story of the people behind that growth. The team that travelled, tasted, argued, and refined until something felt right.

Take a look behind the making of NOICE.

Royan M. | Shilpi Srivastav | Tijil Thomas | Anvesh P | Shakoon Khosla

Building an impactful career means learning how to occupy your space.

When you are aiming for influential roles, it is easy to assume that good work is enough to get noticed. However, thriving in a competitive corporate landscape means learning how to back your ideas with confidence and make your voice heard.

We asked Supriya Shankar, Vice President - Swiggy (General Management), to map out her personal framework for professional authority. Her five core lessons serve as direct mentorship for younger professionals, challenging traditional habits and focusing on building executive presence.

Flip through the slides to see how she reframes everyday workplace dynamics.

Varanasi has been feeding pilgrims, poets and travellers for centuries, and somewhere between the kachoris at dawn and the paan at dusk, every visitor finds a flavour that becomes entirely their own. That is the story we want to help more people discover.

Which is why Swiggy has partnered with the Incredible India, Ministry of Tourism, India and Varanasi Nagar Nigam to launch "Varanasi ka Swaad, Swiggy ke Saath", bringing some of the city's most celebrated eateries to the ghats.

From Kaashi Chaat Bhandar and Chachi ki Prasiddh Kachori to Pahalwan Lassi, Laxmi Chai, Pathan Ji Thandai Waala, Popular Baati Chokha, Taste King, Netaji Paan Bhandar, Gauri Shankar Kachori Wala and Banarasi Paan Mandir, these flavours will now be served to tourists and locals from beautifully designed traditional pushcarts at Namo Ghat, Assi Ghat and Dashashwamedh Ghat. 

The initiative was launched by Shri Yogi Adityanath, Chief Minister Office, Uttar Pradesh, and graced by Shri Ravindra Jaiswal, Honourable Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Stamp, Court Fee and Registration, Uttar Pradesh and MLA, Varanasi North, alongside Rohit Kapoor, CEO, Swiggy Food Marketplace, and senior officials from the Incredible India, Ministry of Tourism, India and Varanasi administration.

This is what it looks like when culture meets convenience.

Rohit Kapoor | Sidharth Bhakoo | Mayur Hola | Vinit Kumar | Neha Singhvi | Ritiin R. Srivastava | Aditya Goswami | Priyank Aggarwal | Mukul Kaura | Akanksha Jain | Akshita Agrawal | Ishita Mehta | Akhila Anil | Surbhi Johri | Aparna Rani | Rosleen Kaur Virdi

Danush Chary’s greatest asset was the curiosity he walked in with.

When Danush joined Instamart four years ago as a POD Picker, he was curious about everything. To satisfy his curiosity, he studied workflows, tracked metrics, and gradually became the person the Hyderabad cluster sent in when a POD was hitting a wall. 

After supporting five new POD launches and turning around two underperforming locations, Danush earned a well-deserved promotion. Exactly four years to the day he first logged in to work, he stepped into the Store Manager role, from picking orders to owning every outcome.

If you want to know what motivated Danush’s growth journey, read his full story through the link in the comments.

Lakkaraju Sai Mahesh
